study.title: Identifying Pathogenesis of Acute Coronary Syndromes using Sequence Contrastive Learning in Coronary Angiography

imaging.modality_detail: X-ray coronary angiography (CAG) videos, Canon INFX-8000C/INFX-8000V flat-panel systems, 15 or 10 fps, converted to 512x512 8-bit and MP4
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries (culprit lesions in LAD, LCx, RCA) in acute coronary syndrome

annotation.annotator_expertise: Experienced cardiologist drew lesion bounding boxes; PR/PE labels from OCT assessed by an experienced interventional cardiologist

task.task_description: Classification of ACS pathogenesis (plaque rupture vs plaque erosion, OCT-confirmed) from cropped culprit-lesion regions of coronary angiography videos, evaluated at frame, video and patient level
task.clinical_application: Non-invasive identification of ACS mechanism from routine CAG to support tailored therapy (e.g., stent deferral in plaque erosion) without intracoronary imaging

temporal_evidence.quote: The neural network has predicted the type of ACS for each individual frame.

method.pretraining: Sequence contrastive pretraining (SeqCon, SimCLR-modified; frames of the same video as positives) followed by transfer learning to classification
method.class_imbalance_handling: Weighted cross-entropy loss and balanced model selection by mean F1-score

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Authors call the test set 'external' but it is a random non-overlapping patient subset (29 patients, 76 videos) from the same single institution

G1.quote: the dataset was modest in size and imbalanced (PR > PE) despite weighting strategies

G2.quote: all data were derived from a single institution, and acquisition protocols, image quality, and vendor differences may affect performance elsewhere

G3.quote: consecutive frames within the same sequence, which share the same underlying pathobiology, are incorrectly treated as negatives

G4.quote: provides only 2-dimensional views of the lumen and is generally considered inadequate for identifying underlying pathology

G6.quote: Prospective studies are required to test whether AI‐assisted angiographic classification can influence management or outcomes.

G8.quote: we will aim to incorporate these nonimaging factors, together with CAG images, to better distinguish PR from PE

G9.quote: excluded less common ACS etiologies such as calcified nodule and spontaneous coronary artery dissection; model behavior in these settings is untested

G11.quote: we did not evaluate clinical decision thresholds or patient outcomes

other_limitations: Ground truth based on OCT interpretation without histopathologic confirmation
Selection bias from requiring interpretable OCT and analyzable angiography
Culprit lesion cropping performed manually; no automated lesion detector
future_work: Stenosis detector to automatically localize culprit lesion for real-time decision aid
Incorporate nonimaging patient factors together with CAG images
Integration into prospective clinical workflows and evaluation of effect on management/outcomes
